question: A manager tells his team to 'use common sense' with Claude rather than writing anything down. What is the most useful thing to recommend he add?
options: A) A requirement that every Claude conversation be saved and forwarded to him so he has a full record.
B) A monthly report of how many messages each person sent, to show that Claude is being used enough.
C) A rule that only the two most experienced people on the team may use Claude for any work purpose.
D) A short written standard naming approved plans, permitted data, disclosure rules and who to ask.
correct_answers: D) A short written standard naming approved plans, permitted data, disclosure rules and who to ask.
explanations: Collecting every conversation creates a large store of sensitive material without telling anyone what is allowed.
Volume statistics measure activity, not whether the activity complied with anything.
Restricting use to two people avoids the question rather than answering it, and does not guide their judgment either.
Correct. A short, concrete standard is what makes a policy usable day to day: what plan, what data, what must be disclosed, and who decides the ambiguous cases.
